findings.description: The Lambda function embeds a static AWS access key ID and secret access key as plaintext environment variables in the Terraform code. These credentials are committed to version control, visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, and stored in Terraform state, enabling credential theft and account compromise.

No kms_key_arn is set, so the environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are readable in plaintext by any principal with basic Lambda read permissions rather than being protected by a customer-managed CMK with its own key policy.

No code_signing_config_arn is configured, so the function's deployment package is not validated against a trusted signing profile, allowing an attacker with lambda:UpdateFunctionCode to deploy unauthorized code.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL controls, which facilitates data exfiltration if the function is compromised.

The assume role policy allows the entire lambda.amazonaws.com service principal to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, leaving the role open to cross-account confused-deputy abuse.
